title: Talking about people
description: Describe someone you know: what they are like and how they treat you.
grammar: adjectives of character, and the verbs that go with them
grammarNote: The adjectives of character agree with the person and go with ser: es amable, es generosa, son ambiciosos.

explanation.summary: To describe a person you need adjectives of character and a few verbs that go with them. These words let you say what someone is really like, which is the difference between a description and a list of facts.

sections.heading: What someone is like
sections.body: The adjectives of character go with ser, because they say what a person is and not what a person is doing. They agree with the person in number and gender: es amable, es generosa, son ambiciosos. An adjective of character can also stand alone after the noun: mi amigo generoso.

examples.es: Mi hermana es generosa y humilde.
examples.en: My sister is generous and humble.

examples.es: Es más paciente de lo que parece.
examples.en: He is more patient than he seems.

sections.heading: How a person acts
sections.body: Some adjectives describe the way someone acts rather than a quality they hold. Es orgulloso, es curioso, es cariñoso: these work with ser in the same way. When you talk about the person rather than the quality, the sentence is short and the adjective does the work.

examples.en: He is proud of his work.
He is curious: he asks about everything.

sections.heading: Trust and distance
sections.body: Confiar is to trust someone, and it always takes a person: confío en ella, confías en mí. Echar de menos is to miss someone: echo de menos a mi familia. The two of them say more about a friendship than any list of adjectives.

examples.en: I trust my friend a lot.

examples.es: Echo de menos a mi familia.

examples.en: We are ambitious and we support each other.

The verb confiar: confío, confías, confía. It takes en: confío en ti.

drills.note: Generoso takes -a for a woman: es generosa.

drills.meaning: we are three very ambitious people
drills.note: Ambicioso takes -as in the plural: son ambiciosas.

drills.prompt: ___ mucho en mi amigo, que nunca me falla.
drills.meaning: I trust my friend a lot, who never lets me down
drills.note: Confiar takes en before the person: confío en él.

drills.prompt: Echo ___ a mi familia, que está muy lejos.
drills.meaning: I miss my family, who is very far away
drills.note: The phrase is echar de menos.

drills.prompt: Mi abuelo es más ___ de lo que parece.
drills.meaning: my grandfather is more patient than he seems
drills.note: Paciente has no other ending: es paciente.
